name: CA-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+13 district fundamentals in a heavily Democratic North Coast seat
Incumbent Jared Huffman running with over $1 million cash on hand
Republican challenger Robin Littau shows no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price Huffman around 96% to win
model.rationale: The district's D+13 lean, Huffman's incumbency, and his roughly $1 million financial advantage over a challenger with no reported fundraising all point to a comfortable Democratic hold, and markets agree at about 96%. With no polls or expert ratings available, the forecast rests on fundamentals, which strongly favor Huffman.
model.watch: Any emergence of polling showing a competitive race or significant outside spending against Huffman would be the first sign this is closer than fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jared Huffman, the Democratic incumbent in California's North Coast district, advanced to the general election against Republican Robin Littau. The district carries a D+13 partisan lean, and Huffman enters the race with a large financial edge, holding more than $1 million in cash after raising nearly $1 million, while Littau shows no reported fundraising. No outside groups are spending against the incumbent.

No public polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbency advantage, and the money gap. Prediction markets price Huffman's chances at roughly 96 percent. All available evidence points to a safe Democratic hold, with the main uncertainty being the absence of direct polling in the district.
